overview: Gallimimus bullatus was the largest ornithomimosaur known at the time of its description — up to six metres long — from the Late Cretaceous Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. Its long arms, toothless beak, three-toed feet and overall proportions are remarkably similar to a large flightless bird, and it is one of the first dinosaurs demonstrated by trackways to have run at speeds exceeding 40 km/h.

Originally interpreted as a filter-feeder (based on presumed comb-like structures in the beak), Gallimimus is now thought to have been an omnivore, taking insects, small vertebrates and plant material in the manner of a modern cassowary. The Jurassic Park herd stampede scene used Gallimimus as the first large-scale computer-generated dinosaur crowd.

fossilSites.name: Nemegt Formation
fossilSites.note: Late Cretaceous fluvial and aeolian deposits preserving Gallimimus alongside Tarbosaurus, ankylosaurs and giant sauropods.

articles.title: Discovery and description
articles.body: Described by Osmólska, Roniewicz and Barsbold in 1972 from material collected by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert. Multiple individuals of different sizes are known. The name means "chicken mimic" referring to superficially bird-like proportions.

articles.title: Locomotion
articles.body: Gallimimus had long, slender hindlimbs with elongate metatarsals — the same configuration seen in fast-running birds. Trackway evidence and muscle-mass estimates suggest running speeds of 40–50 km/h in adults, making it one of the fastest large dinosaurs known. The tail was stiff and horizontal, acting as a counterbalance during locomotion.

articles.title: Diet and behaviour
articles.body: The toothless beak and comparatively small head were originally associated with filter-feeding in water. More recent analyses of jaw mechanics and comparisons with modern omnivorous birds suggest a broader diet of insects, small vertebrates, eggs and plant material. Gallimimus may have formed loose foraging groups similar to ostriches.

fossilRecord.evidence: Long limbs, small head and toothless jaws support ostrich-like locomotion and omnivorous/generalist feeding interpretations.

consensusScope: diet, locomotion and major uncertainty wording

record.mya: early Maastrichtian, roughly 70-68 million years ago
record.description: Gallimimus bullatus was a large, long-limbed ornithomimid from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. Multiple partial and nearly complete skeletons, including skulls and juveniles, document a toothless, cursorially specialised biped.
facts: The jaws were toothless and covered by a beak.
Long hindlimbs support efficient running, but a maximum speed cannot be read directly from fossils.
Diet remains unresolved; proposed plant, small-animal and filter-feeding components are hypotheses.

review.ageReviewNote: The Nemegt Formation is early Maastrichtian in most current schemes, broadly 70-68 Ma.

evidence.material: Multiple partial-to-nearly-complete skeletons with skulls and several growth stages.
evidence.confidenceLimit: Very high for anatomy and bipedality; high for cursorial adaptation; low for exact diet and speed.
